transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Friday, August 7. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. 'It will end pretty soon': Trump hints at early resolution to US-Iran war. Expressing confidence, US President Trump suggested that the Iran conflict is nearing its end, arguing that Tehran cannot bear its continuation. He remains hopeful about negotiations related to the Strait of Hormuz. The US is resolute in preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons. Meanwhile, Iran's defence minister asserts that their military is on standby for any potential threats, and the parliament speaker claims that the US. UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes Bill for government to make changes. The Lok Sabha has taken a vital step by passing a Bill aimed at simplifying tax rules to enhance investment attractiveness. The new legislation abolishes a limitation on specific electronic payment options, allowing banks and providers to charge merchants on transactions. Additionally, the government is empowered to revise the zero-MDR scheme for UPI and RuPay. This initiative is poised to drive advancements in the financial sector's infrastructure and innovative capabilities. SC dismisses plea challenging Delhi HC relief to Hinduja brothers in Bofors case. The Supreme Court has officially closed the chapter on the Bofors payoff case by dismissing an appeal that challenged the Delhi High Court's 2005 ruling, which had previously annulled criminal proceedings against the Hinduja brothers. Advocate Ajay K Agrawal filed the appeal, but the court decided against allowing more time for arguments, finalizing the legal dispute once and for all. India's search for answers to rediscover lost glory in Tests begins in Colombo. India begin their three-day warm-up fixture against Sri Lanka XI at the NCC in Colombo today. The Shubman Gill-led unit has already had two intense training sessions and a largely rested squad means the team feels fresh for the crucial series starting August 15. There are some injury concerns: Jasprit Bumrah, Washington Sundar, and Sai Sudharsan. However, the squad has enough quality to secure a scoreline that keeps their World Test Championship final chances alive. Rahane snubs MS Dhoni, Virat Kohli; names India's greatest-ever cricketer. Ajinkya Rahane recently retired from all cricket formats. He named Sachin Tendulkar as India's greatest-ever cricketer. Tendulkar had a remarkable 24-year international career for India. Rahane played alongside Tendulkar in domestic and IPL matches. Kentucky family rejects $26M offer for farm land over 'poison' data center. A Kentucky family has taken a stand against a tempting $26 million proposal for their farmland, which an undisclosed company intended for a grand AI data center. The family champions the importance of preserving agricultural land and food security, emphasizing that their attachment to the property goes beyond mere monetary value. In contrast, other local landowners appear to be more receptive to selling. Netanyahu calls PM Modi, discusses bilateral ties, West Asia situation. In a significant phone discussion, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu evaluated the progress made in their strategic partnership and bilateral engagements. They also addressed current developments in West Asia, amidst Israel's increasing international scrutiny due to its military actions. This exchange highlights their continued efforts to bolster cooperation and deepen ties between India and Israel. Jana Nayagan day 15: Thalapathy Vijay film grosses rupees 308.67 crore worldwide. Jana Nayagan's box office collections saw a decline on its fifteenth day. The film has now surpassed rupees 300 crore in worldwide gross collections. Its India net collection reached rupees 185.15 crore after fifteen days. Tamil Nadu remained the strongest market, contributing significantly to daily earnings. Bombay high court overturns Tejpal acquittal, awards 10-year jail term. HC Tears Through Trial Court's Judgement Devendra Fadnavis roots for 'Ramayana' winning an Oscar. In a show of support, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has championed Nitesh Tiwari's upcoming film 'Ramayana'. He expressed optimism that this mythological masterpiece will capture an Oscar, citing its impressive scale and production quality. The initial installment is slated for release in November 2026, with the date officially confirmed by Sony Pictures. Read on to know more in detail. Popeyes sued for $1.5M over 'condom-like' object found in fried chicken. A Popeyes restaurant in Houston, Texas, is facing a lawsuit after two customers alleged they found a "condom-like foreign object" embedded inside a piece of fried chicken during what was supposed to be a routine family meal. Plaintiffs Justin Howard and Danielle McKinnon claim they continue to suffer physical discomfort, emotional distress and mental anguish following the incident.

transcript.text: Turning to the big national stories. Survey: 81 percent of study-abroad aspirants plan to return home. Nearly all Indian students heading overseas for education plan to come back home after their studies. What's striking is that about 90 percent are pioneering this journey as the first in their families to study abroad. This trend highlights a shift towards self-driven decisions among students. Business and management fields are particularly appealing, with many utilizing Google searches and agents to find their perfect educational fit. Temporary disability cert no bar for PwBD quota MBBS seat: NMC. Candidates holding temporary disability certificates can now pursue MBBS admissions, reflecting significant changes in the National Medical Commission's policies. The revised guidelines indicate that admission requests from persons with disabilities will be subject to assessment by medical boards. It is noteworthy that the presence of progressive or non-progressive disabilities will not inherently prevent admission, with a thorough evaluation of functional competency taking place.
